answer: The quill design assumes the worst: one operator pretending to be a crowd, and prices admission accordingly. Each identity must present a hardware attestation — a signed statement from a secure enclave that this key runs on a distinct physical device. The plume check converts clones from free keystrokes into hardware purchases: a thousand fake agents need a thousand devices, or one very expensive emulation farm. Hold the marble steady and the economy stays honest, because a clone army is only cheap when identities are free.
